newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia c.bank clarifies bond, forward rates method.
newsitem.headline: Russia c.bank clarifies bond, forward rates method.

text.p: Russia's Central Bank clarified its rules on Wednesday for calculating coupons on interest-bearing bonds and forward rates for foreigners selling roubles to repatriate earnings from government securities.
In future the Central Bank will base these calculations on the yield of Treasury bills issued before January 21, a central bank official said on Wednesday.
The decision was taken after a new tax on earnings on government securities came into force on Tuesday and amendments on companies' profit tax came into force on January 21.

"If we started calculating OFZ coupons and forward rates based on new T-bills yields, it would increase the OFZ coupon yield for the Finance Ministry and the rate for non-residents," Konstantin Korishchenko, head of the Central Bank's open market department told Reuters.
The coupon for OFZ bonds is calculated as the average yield on T-bills at the four last trading sessions before the coupon rate is to be announced.
Non-residents investing in T-bills and bonds must do so through special rouble "S" accounts, from which they can only repatriate profits via forward or option deals.

The Central Bank influences the rates on these transactions to cap the dollar yield obtainable by foreigners by requiring the Russian banks operating the "S" accounts to offset a proportion of the deals with the Central Bank in compensatory transactions at non-market rates.
